title: Concerns of traffic rise as Sikes Senter project continues - NewsBreak
text: WICHITA FALLS ( KFDX/KJTL ) — As Sikes Senter Mall is right off Midwestern Parkway, residents say traffic concerns are on their radar. Many business owners and residents around the area are on board with the upcoming project and believe that more traffic will be a good thing, not just for local stores but for Wichita Falls as a whole. “It’s all about traffic when you’re in business, you’re looking for more people to get out here and the mall has dwindled in traffic, it use to be why you’d be in the mall because of traffic,” said Joe Shaffer, the co-owner of Next Level Golf. “I have no problem with the new stadium and shopping center coming in over there, I think it’s progress, I think it’s going to be good for the area as far as the traffic goes. All traffic is going to do is bring more customers to everyone around,” said Kenny Bond owner of K. Bond Jewlers. Other residents think that more traffic can cause more issues than it can benefit. “There’s just so much going on in this intersection already,” said local tattoo artist Myranda Martinez. “I feel like it is a place that people go to shop, eat, and do things like that. I feel like the stadium would really disrupt that energy.” “Me personally, if im in an area and that traffic is heavy im just not gonna go. Divert plans and do something different, I’m not gonna do what I was gonna do if the traffic is too heavy,” said resident Rebekah Sinegail. “I think they need to do it somewhere else.” The area will have about six to seven entrances to help mitigate traffic. Ron Kitchens, CEO of Wichita Falls Chamber of Commerce, said the direction of the road will allow smoother traffic on Midwestern Parkway. “I think that’s part of it in the redevelopment, you have to look at traffic mitigation and what that looks like. Preliminarily, we’re talking about a road that would go down the center,” said Kitchens. “So that’s going to give you access different access points, so people aren’t coming in the same entrances. And it would be parallel roads, as well so that you would so you’re going to mitigate where people are entering.” But nearby neighborhoods could face new pressures from overflow parking and increased congestion. As the city prepares for its public hearing on August 14, residents say they just want to be heard about any and all concerns regarding Sikes Senter.
